top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu alone) is my preferred proposal on the common literary criteria. Judging from public descriptions of Blinding (the Orbitor trilogy) and Solenoid, and not from independent verification or close reading, I find a recognisable voice built on long, patterned sentences and recurring images. It shows formal control across very large structures and joins memory, the body and dream into one imaginative and intellectual project. The citation scope is clean: one writer, one language, prose as the load-bearing element with poetry named as its root and not as a separately assessed body of work. That wording fits what translated evidence can support. Important uncertainties remain. Romanian rhythm, syntax and sonic patterning cannot be checked through translation. Whether the late novels deepen the early project or partly repeat it is unresolved. Coverage of the poetry and early prose in translation is thin. These reservations limit how firmly I hold the whole-oeuvre claim, but they do not show a failure of any stated criterion, so I rank this proposal above no award (P000). The unanimous round-2 support is not treated as evidence of merit.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; the profile records no personal, professional or institutional tie to the proposed laureate. My scholarly interests in the fragment, exile literature and Celan translation overlap thematically with alternatives such as Carson and Zurita, but not with the sole proposal on the slate. This is context only and is not adjudicated.
